blocks.en: Chapala Theological Seminary, a ministry of Common Ground Fellowship | Professor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers

blocks.en: This course is drawn from the worship curriculum of Dr. Wayne Cook, who served eleven years as Professor of Pastoral Ministries and Preaching, together with the teaching of Andi Cook, who taught alongside him at the seminary. It reflects not only academic study but decades of pastoral and seminary experience.
blocks.es_reference: Este curso proviene del currículo de adoración del Dr. Wayne Cook, quien sirvió once años como Profesor de Ministerios Pastorales y Predicación, junto con la enseñanza de Andi Cook, quien enseñó a su lado en el seminario. Refleja no solo el estudio académico sino décadas de experiencia pastoral y de seminario.

blocks.en: I. Planning Around the Moods
blocks.es_reference: I. Planear alrededor de los ánimos

blocks.en: A worship service is not a random pile of songs, prayers, and announcements thrown together at the last minute. It is planned, and it is planned around moods or motifs. There are five such moods, and they give the service its shape and its movement. The worship leader's task is to examine these moods and decide how and where to use each one, so that the service builds rather than wanders. A service planned around the moods has unity and progression; a service thrown together has neither.
blocks.es_reference: Un servicio de adoración no es un montón aleatorio de cánticos, oraciones, y anuncios juntados a último minuto. Es planeado, y se planea alrededor de ánimos o motivos. Hay cinco de estos ánimos, y dan al servicio su forma y su movimiento. La tarea del líder de adoración es examinar estos ánimos y decidir cómo y dónde usar cada uno, para que el servicio se construya en lugar de divagar. Un servicio planeado alrededor de los ánimos tiene unidad y progresión; un servicio juntado al azar no tiene ninguna.

blocks.en: II. Recognition, Praise, and Confession
blocks.es_reference: II. Reconocimiento, alabanza, y confesión

blocks.en: The first mood is recognition, sometimes called adoration or vision. It is first of all God's recognition of us. Read Isaiah 6, where the prophet sees the Lord high and lifted up. We enter recognition through silence and meditation, through a call to worship, and through an invocation. This is where the service properly begins, with the awe of standing before the holy God.
blocks.es_reference: El primer ánimo es el reconocimiento, a veces llamado adoración o visión. Es ante todo el reconocimiento de Dios hacia nosotros. Lea Isaías 6, donde el profeta ve al Señor alto y sublime. Entramos en el reconocimiento por medio del silencio y la meditación, por medio de un llamado a la adoración, y por medio de una invocación. Aquí es donde el servicio propiamente comienza, con el asombro de estar ante el Dios santo.

blocks.en: The second mood is praise or thanksgiving. Through hymns, prayers, and Scriptures we glorify God. Genuine gratitude rises from the soul as God satisfies our hunger; we thank Him for His love, for life itself, and for the necessities of life. The third mood is confession. In confession we see ourselves as God sees us and we agree with Him about our sin, as 1 John 1:9 teaches, longing for cleansing. Notice that Isaiah confessed only after he had seen God's holiness, recognition leads naturally to confession. And confession should be specific, not general. David understood that any sin is finally a sin against God.
blocks.es_reference: El segundo ánimo es la alabanza o acción de gracias. Por medio de himnos, oraciones, y Escrituras glorificamos a Dios. La gratitud genuina surge del alma a medida que Dios satisface nuestra hambre; le agradecemos por Su amor, por la vida misma, y por las necesidades de la vida. El tercer ánimo es la confesión. En la confesión nos vemos como Dios nos ve y concordamos con Él sobre nuestro pecado, como enseña 1 Juan 1:9, anhelando limpieza. Note que Isaías confesó solo después de haber visto la santidad de Dios; el reconocimiento lleva naturalmente a la confesión. Y la confesión debe ser específica, no general. David entendió que todo pecado es finalmente un pecado contra Dios.

blocks.en: III. Illumination and Dedication
blocks.es_reference: III. Iluminación y dedicación

blocks.en: The fourth mood is illumination or proclamation. This is the moment when God moves us, and it is accomplished above all through the reading of Scripture and through preaching, though drama, the children's sermon, and testimony may serve it too. Here we must remember a key distinction: teaching touches the mind, but preaching touches the mind, the heart, and the will. Illumination is meant to move the whole person.
blocks.es_reference: El cuarto ánimo es la iluminación o proclamación. Este es el momento cuando Dios nos mueve, y se logra sobre todo por medio de la lectura de la Escritura y por medio de la predicación, aunque el drama, el sermón para niños, y el testimonio pueden servirlo también. Aquí debemos recordar una distinción clave: la enseñanza toca la mente, pero la predicación toca la mente, el corazón, y la voluntad. La iluminación está destinada a mover a toda la persona.

blocks.en: The fifth mood is dedication or consecration. Here we give back to God, and it normally comes in two places. In the offering we dedicate our resources; in the invitation we offer ourselves. Both are acts of returning to God what we first received from Him. Notice how the moods carry the worshipper on a journey: we recognize God, we praise Him, we confess our sin, we are moved by His word, and we dedicate ourselves back to Him. That is the architecture of a service.
blocks.es_reference: El quinto ánimo es la dedicación o consagración. Aquí devolvemos a Dios, y normalmente viene en dos lugares. En la ofrenda dedicamos nuestros recursos; en la invitación nos ofrecemos a nosotros mismos. Ambos son actos de devolver a Dios lo que primero recibimos de Él. Note cómo los ánimos llevan al adorador en un viaje: reconocemos a Dios, lo alabamos, confesamos nuestro pecado, somos movidos por Su palabra, y nos dedicamos de vuelta a Él. Esa es la arquitectura de un servicio.

blocks.en: IV. Extremes, Counsels, and Principles
blocks.es_reference: IV. Extremos, consejos, y principios

blocks.en: There are two extremes to avoid in planning. One is rigid formalism, a burdensome structure that quenches the Spirit. The other is pure spontaneity with no order at all. As the old saying goes, if I am your leader, which way do we go? Worship needs both dignity and planning; wisdom lies in the balance. A few counsels help: involve your people in the music, the message, and the planning; make use of seasonal events without being a slave to the calendar; provide variety, but change gradually, for people need the familiar; and make sure all the facilities and people are ready before the service begins.
blocks.es_reference: Hay dos extremos que evitar en la planeación. Uno es el formalismo rígido, una estructura pesada que apaga al Espíritu. El otro es la pura espontaneidad sin ningún orden. Como dice el viejo dicho, si yo soy su líder, ¿por dónde vamos? La adoración necesita tanto dignidad como planeación; la sabiduría está en el balance. Algunos consejos ayudan: involucre a su pueblo en la música, el mensaje, y la planeación; haga uso de los eventos de temporada sin ser esclavo del calendario; provea variedad, pero cambie gradualmente, porque la gente necesita lo familiar; y asegúrese de que todas las instalaciones y personas estén listas antes de que comience el servicio.

blocks.en: Five principles guide good planning. Unity means the whole service is one and every element fits together. Order means real structure, accomplished with an order of service. Proportion means giving each part the right amount of time. Movement means the service moves forward, building toward something. And climax means the service reaches a high point, ideally the invitation. Finally, the one who leads must prepare himself spiritually and emotionally, pray ahead of time, come enthusiastic and joyful so the people catch that spirit, dress appropriately, and let the congregation see him genuinely worshipping. People will not follow a leader who is merely managing a program.
blocks.es_reference: Cinco principios guían la buena planeación. La unidad significa que todo el servicio es uno y cada elemento encaja. El orden significa estructura real, lograda con un orden de servicio. La proporción significa dar a cada parte la cantidad correcta de tiempo. El movimiento significa que el servicio avanza, construyendo hacia algo. Y el clímax significa que el servicio alcanza un punto culminante, idealmente la invitación. Finalmente, el que dirige debe prepararse espiritual y emocionalmente, orar de antemano, venir entusiasta y gozoso para que la gente capte ese espíritu, vestir apropiadamente, y dejar que la congregación lo vea adorando genuinamente. La gente no seguirá a un líder que meramente está administrando un programa.

sa.prompt: Worship is planned around five moods or motifs. Explain what this means for structuring a service.
sa.model: Planning a service around five moods or motifs means the worship leader deliberately decides how and where to use each mood — recognition, praise, confession, illumination, and dedication — so the service builds and moves rather than being a random pile of songs, prayers, and announcements thrown together. A service structured this way has unity and progression, carrying the worshipper on a deliberate journey rather than wandering aimlessly.

sa.prompt: Explain the first mood, recognition (adoration), using Isaiah 6. How is it accomplished in a service?
sa.model: Recognition, sometimes called adoration or vision, is first of all God's recognition of us — illustrated in Isaiah 6, where the prophet sees the Lord high and lifted up. It is accomplished in a service through silence and meditation, through a call to worship, and through an invocation, forming the proper beginning point where the service opens with awe before the holy God.

sa.prompt: Explain the second mood, praise or thanksgiving, and how it is expressed in the service.
sa.model: Praise or thanksgiving is expressed through hymns, prayers, and Scriptures by which we glorify God, with genuine gratitude rising from the soul as God satisfies our hunger. We thank Him for His love, for life itself, and for the necessities of life, moving the service from mere awe into active, voiced gratitude.

sa.prompt: Explain the third mood, confession, using Isaiah and David. Why should confession be specific?
sa.model: In confession we see ourselves as God sees us and agree with Him about our sin, as 1 John 1:9 teaches, longing for cleansing. Isaiah confessed only after seeing God's holiness, showing that recognition leads naturally to confession. Confession should be specific rather than general because David understood that any sin, however seemingly small, is finally a sin against God Himself, requiring honest, named repentance rather than vague acknowledgment.

sa.prompt: Explain the fourth mood, illumination or proclamation. How does preaching differ from teaching?
sa.model: Illumination or proclamation is the moment when God moves us, accomplished above all through the reading of Scripture and preaching, though drama, the children's sermon, and testimony may serve it too. Preaching differs from teaching because teaching touches the mind, but preaching touches the mind, the heart, and the will — illumination is meant to move the whole person, not just inform it.

sa.prompt: Explain the fifth mood, dedication or consecration, and the two places it normally occurs.
sa.model: Dedication or consecration is where we give back to God, and it normally comes in two places: in the offering, where we dedicate our resources, and in the invitation, where we offer ourselves. Both are acts of returning to God what we first received from Him, completing the journey the moods have carried the worshipper through.

sa.prompt: Explain the two extremes in planning a worship service and why balance is needed.
sa.model: The two extremes to avoid are rigid formalism, a burdensome structure that quenches the Spirit, and pure spontaneity with no order at all, which leaves people not knowing which way to go. Balance is needed because worship requires both dignity and planning — too much structure kills life, and too little structure creates confusion, so wisdom lies in holding both together.

sa.prompt: Give the counsels for planning worship, including involving the people and providing variety.
sa.model: The counsels for planning worship include: involve your people in the music, the message, and the planning; make use of seasonal events without being a slave to the calendar; provide variety, but change gradually since people need the familiar; and make sure all the facilities and people are ready before the service begins.

sa.prompt: Explain the five principles of planning: unity, order, proportion, movement, and climax.
sa.model: Unity means the whole service is one and every element fits together; order means real structure, accomplished with an order of service; proportion means giving each part the right amount of time; movement means the service moves forward, building toward something; and climax means the service reaches a high point, ideally the invitation. Together these five principles keep a service from feeling scattered or aimless.

sa.prompt: How should the worship leader prepare himself and conduct himself when leading the service?
sa.model: The worship leader must prepare himself spiritually and emotionally, pray ahead of time, and come enthusiastic and joyful so the people catch that spirit. He should dress appropriately and let the congregation see him genuinely worshipping rather than merely managing a program, since people will not follow a leader who is only running through motions rather than actually engaged with God.
